bitcoin.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
bitcoin.def: Digital money with no central issuer, run by a public network since its first block on 3 January 2009. The protocol caps the supply at 21 million coins.

satoshi.name: Satoshi (sat)
satoshi.def: The smallest unit of bitcoin: 1 BTC = 100,000,000 sats.

21-million.name: 21 million cap
21-million.def: The protocol's hard limit on the bitcoin supply. New coins enter only through the block reward, which halves every 210,000 blocks.

blockchain.name: Blockchain
blockchain.def: Bitcoin's public ledger: a chain of blocks in which every block points to the one before it. A new block arrives about every 10 minutes on average.

proof-of-work.name: Proof of work
proof-of-work.def: How miners compete to add the next block by spending computing power. It makes rewriting past blocks expensive.

node.name: Node
node.def: Software that keeps its own copy of the blockchain and checks every rule itself, so you do not have to trust anyone else's copy.

bitcoin-only.name: Bitcoin-only
bitcoin-only.def: Covering Bitcoin and nothing else: no altcoins, no tokens. Virtuse has been Bitcoin-only since 2022.

self-custody.name: Self-custody
self-custody.def: You hold the keys to your bitcoin yourself. Nobody can freeze or lose them for you, and recovery is your job.

private-key.name: Private key
private-key.def: The secret that authorises spending. Whoever has it controls the coins.

seed-phrase.name: Seed phrase
seed-phrase.def: Usually 12 or 24 words from which every key in a wallet can be restored. Never type it into a website or keep it in a photo app.

passphrase.name: Passphrase
passphrase.def: An optional extra word added to a seed phrase. A different passphrase restores a different wallet, so without the right one the coins do not appear.

hardware-wallet.name: Hardware wallet
hardware-wallet.def: A small device that keeps keys offline and signs transactions without showing the keys to your computer.

cold-storage.name: Cold storage
cold-storage.def: Keys that never touch a device connected to the internet.

multisig.name: Multisig
multisig.def: A wallet that needs several keys to spend, for example 2 of 3, so one lost or stolen key is not the end.

assisted-custody.name: Assisted custody
assisted-custody.def: Multisig in which you hold most keys and a provider holds one to help with recovery and heirs. The provider cannot move the coins alone.

custodian.name: Custodian
custodian.def: A company that holds keys for you, such as an exchange or a regulated custodian. Convenient, but you rely on it.

non-custodial.name: Non-custodial
non-custodial.def: A service that never holds your funds or keys. Virtuse is a non-custodial hub: partners provide the services under their own licences.

proof-of-reserves.name: Proof of reserves
proof-of-reserves.def: A check that a custodian holds the coins it says it holds. It only means something if the liabilities are shown too.

inheritance-plan.name: Bitcoin inheritance plan
inheritance-plan.def: What your heirs need to find, reach and move your bitcoin, without exposing the keys while you are alive.

utxo.name: UTXO
utxo.def: Unspent transaction output: the pieces of bitcoin a wallet actually holds. Many small UTXOs make later transactions more expensive.

mempool.name: Mempool
mempool.def: The queue of transactions waiting to get into a block. When it is full, fees rise.

transaction-fee.name: Transaction fee
transaction-fee.def: What you pay miners to include a transaction, priced in sats per virtual byte (sat/vB), not by the amount sent. Partner buying fees are a different thing: see the Fee Index.

halving.name: Halving
halving.def: Every 210,000 blocks, about four years, the new-coin reward per block is cut in half. The halving at block 840,000 on 20 April 2024 cut it to 3.125 BTC.

hashrate.name: Hashrate
hashrate.def: The total computing power securing the network.

difficulty-adjustment.name: Difficulty adjustment
difficulty-adjustment.def: Every 2,016 blocks the network resets how hard mining is, so that blocks keep arriving about every 10 minutes.

mining.name: Mining
mining.def: Running specialised machines that do proof of work to earn new bitcoin and transaction fees.

lightning-network.name: Lightning Network
lightning-network.def: A layer on top of Bitcoin for fast, low-fee payments through payment channels.

dca.name: DCA (dollar-cost averaging)
dca.def: Buying a fixed euro amount on a schedule instead of all at once.

drawdown.name: Drawdown
drawdown.def: The fall from a previous peak. On month-end closes Bitcoin fell 70% or more four times between 2011 and 2022, which is why Verdict tests a plan against a 70% fall.

spot-bitcoin-etf.name: Spot Bitcoin ETF
spot-bitcoin-etf.def: A US-listed fund that holds bitcoin. The SEC approved the first ones on 10 January 2024. You own fund shares, not bitcoin or keys.

bitcoin-etp.name: Bitcoin ETP
bitcoin-etp.def: An exchange-traded product that tracks the price of bitcoin and trades on a stock exchange. You hold a security, not bitcoin or keys.

treasury-company.name: Bitcoin treasury company
treasury-company.def: A listed company that holds bitcoin on its balance sheet as a reserve asset.

fear-greed-index.name: Fear & Greed Index
fear-greed-index.def: A sentiment gauge for bitcoin from 0 to 100: 0 means extreme fear, 100 extreme greed.

200-week-ma.name: 200-week moving average
200-week-ma.def: Bitcoin's average price over the last 200 weeks, a long-term trend line.

bitcoin-dominance.name: Bitcoin dominance
bitcoin-dominance.def: Bitcoin's share of the total market value of all crypto-assets.

bitcoin-backed-loan.name: Bitcoin-backed loan (LTV)
bitcoin-backed-loan.def: Borrowing against bitcoin instead of selling it. LTV (loan-to-value) is the loan as a share of the collateral; if the price falls far enough, the collateral can be sold off (liquidation).

mica.name: MiCA
mica.def: The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (EU) 2023/1114. Crypto-asset service providers need an EU authorisation; the national transition periods ended on 1 July 2026 at the latest.

casp.name: CASP
casp.def: Crypto-asset service provider: a firm authorised under MiCA by a national authority. One authorisation lets it serve the whole EU (passporting). You can check a firm in the ESMA register.

travel-rule.name: Travel Rule
travel-rule.def: Since 30 December 2024, Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 requires sender and recipient details to travel with crypto transfers between providers. For a transfer exceeding €1,000 to or from a self-hosted wallet, the provider must take adequate measures to assess that the customer owns or controls that wallet.

dac8.name: DAC8
dac8.def: EU tax directive (EU) 2023/2226. Since 1 January 2026, crypto-asset service providers record your identity, tax number and transactions and report them to the tax authorities. The first exchange between countries is due within nine months after the end of 2026, by 30 September 2027.

amlr.name: AMLR and AMLA
amlr.def: The EU anti-money-laundering regulation (EU) 2024/1624 applies from 10 July 2027. From then, credit institutions, financial institutions and CASPs may not keep anonymous crypto-asset accounts or accounts that anonymise transactions, including through anonymity-enhancing coins. This concerns accounts at providers, not coins in your own wallet. AMLA, the new EU anti-money-laundering authority, has its seat in Frankfurt am Main.

kyc.name: KYC
kyc.def: Know your customer: the identity checks a regulated provider must carry out before it opens an account or carries out a transaction for you.

digital-euro.name: Digital euro
digital-euro.def: A proposed digital form of cash that the ECB would issue. It has not been adopted. On 9 July 2026 the European Parliament agreed to start negotiations with the Council. The ECB says that if EU lawmakers adopt the regulation in the course of 2026, the digital euro could be issued during 2029.

vat-exemption.name: VAT on bitcoin
vat-exemption.def: Exchanging euros for bitcoin and back is exempt from VAT in the EU, the EU Court of Justice ruled in the Hedqvist case (C-264/14) on 22 October 2015.

taxable-event.name: Taxable event
taxable-event.def: What triggers tax on bitcoin. Rules differ by country: in Slovakia both a sale and a swap into another crypto-asset are taxable, while in Poland a swap between crypto-assets is not.

holding-period.name: Holding-period exemption
holding-period.def: Some countries stop taxing a gain once you have held the bitcoin long enough. Czechia does after more than three years; which other countries do is in the country tax guides.

tax-slovakia.name: Bitcoin tax in Slovakia
tax-slovakia.def: Income from selling a crypto-asset is taxable "other income" under section 8(1)(t) of the Income Tax Act, and if your costs are higher than the income, the difference is not taken into account. Rates and the tax return: see the Slovakia guide.

tax-czechia.name: Bitcoin tax in Czechia
tax-czechia.def: A gain is tax-free once you have held the crypto-asset for more than 3 years (capped at CZK 40 million a year together with some other exempt income), or if your total crypto-asset sale proceeds in the year are at most CZK 100,000. Neither applies to business assets.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.def: How fast prices rise, usually measured year on year. It erodes cash, and it is one reason people hold bitcoin.

cpi.name: CPI
cpi.def: The US Consumer Price Index from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the inflation figure markets watch most.

hicp.name: HICP
hicp.def: The euro area's harmonised index of consumer prices, published by Eurostat. The ECB aims for 2% inflation over the medium term.

fed-funds-rate.name: Fed funds rate
fed-funds-rate.def: The US central bank's key interest rate, which the FOMC sets as a target range.

ecb-deposit-rate.name: ECB deposit facility rate
ecb-deposit-rate.def: The rate banks earn on overnight deposits with the Eurosystem, the rate the ECB uses to steer monetary policy.

us-10y.name: US 10-year yield
us-10y.def: What the US government pays to borrow for 10 years, a benchmark for the cost of money worldwide.

real-yield.name: Real yield
real-yield.def: The yield on inflation-protected bonds, roughly a bond yield minus expected inflation. When real yields rise, holding assets that pay no interest, like gold or bitcoin, costs more.

dxy.name: DXY (US dollar index)
dxy.def: The value of the dollar against six major currencies. The euro has the largest weight.

m2.name: M2 money supply
m2.def: Cash, deposits and other liquid money in an economy. Its growth is a common gauge of liquidity.

qe-qt.name: QE / QT
qe-qt.def: Quantitative easing, when a central bank buys bonds and adds money to the system, and quantitative tightening, its reverse.
